text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 LKQ CORPORATION ANNOUNCES RESULTS FOR THIRD QUARTER 2026 Antioch, TENN (October 29, 2026) -- LKQ Corporation (Nasdaq: LKQ) today reported third quarter 2026 financial results. Commenting on the third quarter, John Mendel, Chairman of the Board of LKQ, said: “LKQ remains a fundamentally strong enterprise, supported by its scale, leading positions across key markets, and global distribution platform. At the same time, our recent financial and operating performance has not reflected the strength of the business or met the standards we expect, particularly in Europe. The Board has been deeply engaged in addressing these challenges, and the appointment of a new CEO, leadership changes in Europe, and the engagement of Alvarez & Marsal are important steps in a broader effort to improve execution and financial performance. We believe LKQ has significant strengths that are not currently reflected in its operating performance, and our focus is on translating those strengths into improved performance and increased value for our shareholders.” Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $3.3 billion, a decrease of 5.1% compared to $3.5 billion for the third quarter of 2025. Total parts and services revenue decreased 5.6%, which included a 5.4% decrease in parts and services organic revenue, a 0.7% decrease from foreign exchange rates year over year, and the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures, which increased revenue by 0.6%. Net loss 2 was $24 million, including $111 million of pre-tax non-cash impairment charges, compared to net income of $178 million for the same period of 2025. Diluted loss per share 2 was $(0.09) compared to diluted earnings per share 2 of $0.69 for the same period of 2025. On an adjusted basis, net income 1,2 was $127 million compared to $216 million for the same period of 2025. Adjusted diluted earnings per share 1,2 was $0.50 compared to $0.84 for the same period of 2025. “The third quarter was characterized by weakness in our Europe segment, driven by operational issues related to the ERP implementation in Germany and volume declines in the United Kingdom and Benelux. Specialty was modestly below plan. North America performed in line with expectations despite a softer demand environment,” said Rick Galloway, Chief Financial Officer of LKQ. Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Cash flow from operations 3 and free cash flow 1,3 were $411 million and $372 million, respectively, for the third quarter of 2026. Cash flow from operations 3 and free cash flow 1,3 were $466 million and $336 million, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, the balance sheet reflected total debt of $3.7 billion and total leverage, as defined in our credit facility, was 2.8x EBITDA. Returning Capital to Shareholders During the third quarter of 2026, the Company invested $30 million to repurchase 1.2 million shares of its common stock and distributed $76 million in cash dividends. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company returned $313 million to its shareholders by investing $83 million to repurchase 3.1 million shares of its common stock and distributing $230 million in cash dividends. Since initiating the stock repurchase program in late October 2018, the Company has repurchased approximately 72 million shares of its common stock for a total of $3.0 billion through September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, there was $1.5 billion remaining on the authorization. (1) Non-GAAP measure. On October 25, 2026, the Board authorized a two-year extension to its stock repurchase program, authorizing repurchases through October 25, 2028. On October 27, 2026, the Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.30 per share of common stock, payable on December 3, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 19, 2026. Strategic Review Alongside the recent leadership changes, the Board has decided to suspend the strategic review, including the Specialty segment sales process. This will provide the new leadership team the opportunity to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the business and evaluate the full range of value‑creation pathways available to the Company. The Board will continue to oversee the strategic direction, protect shareholder interests, and ensure accountability. This includes evaluating opportunities that it believes could enhance shareholder value and optimize the Company’s strategic positioning over the long term. Other Events On October 23, 2026, the Company announced that the Board appointed Salvatore A. “Sal” Abbate as President and Chief Executive Officer, effective December 15, 2026. Mr. Abbate brings more than three decades of experience leading large, complex distribution and industrial businesses. As CEO of Veritiv Corporation, he led a significant transformation of the company, with its share price increasing more than 13-fold during his tenure, culminating in its $2.6 billion sale to Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2023. Before becoming CEO, he served as Veritiv’s Chief Operating Officer and Chief Commercial Officer. Earlier in his career, Mr. Abbate held senior leadership roles at Andersen Windows & Doors, Solutia, Inc., now part of Eastman Chemical Company, and Armstrong World Industries, with responsibilities spanning sales, marketing, distribution, logistics, manufacturing, strategy and process improvement. On October 23, 2026 the Company announced that it is withdrawing its full-year 2026 guidance, which was most recently updated on July 30, 2026. About LKQ Corporation LKQ Corporation (www.lkqcorp.com) is a leading provider of alternative and specialty parts to repair and accessorize automobiles and other vehicles. LKQ has operations in North America, Europe and Taiwan. LKQ offers its customers a broad range of OEM recycled and aftermarket parts, replacement systems, components, equipment, and services to repair and accessorize automobiles, trucks, and recreational and performance vehicles. These factors include the following (not necessarily in order of importance): • our operating results and financial condition have been and could continue to be adversely affected by the economic, political and social conditions in North America, Europe, Taiwan and other countries, as well as the economic health of vehicle owners and numbers and types of vehicles sold; • we face competition from local, national, international, and internet-based vehicle products providers, and this competition could negatively affect our business; • we rely upon insurance companies and our customers to promote the usage of alternative parts; • intellectual property claims relating to aftermarket products could adversely affect our business; • if the number of vehicles involved in accidents or being repaired declines, or the mix of the types of vehicles in the overall vehicle population changes, our business could suffer; • fluctuations in the prices of commodities could adversely affect our financial results; • an adverse change in our relationships with our suppliers, disruption to our supply of inventory, or the misconduct, performance failures or negligence of our third party vendors or service providers could increase our expenses, impede our ability to serve our customers, or expose us to liability; • future public health emergencies could have a material adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity, the nature and extent of which is highly uncertain; • if we determine that our goodwill or other intangible assets have become impaired, we may incur significant charges to our pretax income; • we could be subject to product liability claims and involved in product recalls; • we may not be able to successfully acquire businesses or integrate acquisitions, and we may not be able to successfully divest certain businesses; • we have a substantial amount of indebtedness, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and our ability to obtain financing in the future and to react to changes in our business; • our senior notes do not impose any limitations on our ability to incur additional debt or protect against certain other types of transactions, and we may incur certain additional indebtedness under our credit agreement and CAD Note; • each of our credit agreement and CAD Note imposes operating and financial restrictions on us and our subsidiaries, which may prevent us from capitalizing on business opportunities; • we may not be able to generate sufficient cash to service all of our indebtedness, and may be forced to take other actions to satisfy our obligations under our indebtedness, which may not be successful; • our future capital needs may require that we seek to refinance our debt or obtain additional debt or equity financing, events that could have a negative effect on our business; • our variable rate indebtedness subjects us to interest rate risk, which could cause our indebtedness service obligations to increase significantly; • repayment of our indebtedness is dependent on cash flow generated by our subsidiaries; • a downgrade in our credit rating would impact us; • the amount and frequency of our share repurchases and dividend payments may fluctuate; • existing or new laws and regulations, or changes to enforcement or interpretation of existing laws or regulations, may prohibit, restrict or burden the sale of aftermarket, recycled, refurbished or remanufactured products; • we are subject to environmental regulations and incur costs relating to environmental matters; • if we fail to maintain proper and effective internal control over financial reporting in the future, our ability to produce accurate and timely financial statements could be negatively impacted, which could harm our operating results and investor perceptions of our company and as a result may have a material adverse effect on the value of our common stock; • we may be adversely affected by legal, regulatory or market responses to global climate change; • our amended and restated bylaws provide that the courts in the State of Delaware are the exclusive forums for substantially all disputes between us and our stockholders, which could limit our stockholders’ ability to obtain a favorable judicial forum for disputes with us or our directors, officers or employees; • our effective tax rate could materially increase as a consequence of various factors, including U.S. and/or international tax legislation, applicable interpretations and administrative guidance, our mix of earnings by jurisdiction, and U.S. and foreign jurisdictional audits; • if significant tariffs or other restrictions are placed on products or materials we import or any related counter-measures are taken by countries to which we export products, our revenue and results of operations may be materially harmed; • governmental agencies may refuse to grant or renew our operating licenses and permits; • the costs of complying with the requirements of laws pertaining to data privacy and cybersecurity of personal information and the potential liability associated with the failure to comply with such laws could materially adversely affect our business and results of operations; • our employees are important to successfully manage our business and achieve our objectives; • we operate in foreign jurisdictions, which exposes us to foreign exchange and other risks; • our business may be adversely affected by union activities and labor and employment laws; • we rely on information technology and communication systems in critical areas of our operations and a disruption relating to such technology and systems, including cybersecurity threats, could harm our business; • business interruptions in our distribution centers or other facilities may affect our operations, the function of our computer systems, and/or the availability and distribution of merchandise, which may affect our business; • if we experience problems with our fleet of trucks and other vehicles, our business could be harmed; • we may lose the right to operate at key locations; and • activist investors could cause us to incur substantial costs, divert management’s attention, and have an adverse effect on our business. We calculate Segment EBITDA as Net Income and Loss excluding net income and loss attributable to noncontrolling interest; income and loss from discontinued operations; depreciation; amortization; interest; gains and losses on debt extinguishment; income tax expense; restructuring and transaction related expenses; change in fair value of contingent consideration liabilities; other gains and losses related to acquisitions, equity method investments, or divestitures; equity in losses and earnings of unconsolidated subsidiaries; equity investment fair value adjustments; impairment charges; and direct impacts of the Ukraine/Russia conflict. Our chief operating decision maker ("CODM"), who is our Chief Executive Officer, uses Segment EBITDA as the key measure of our segment profit or loss. The CODM uses Segment EBITDA to compare profitability among our segments and evaluate business strategies. This financial measure is included in the metrics used to determine incentive compensation for our senior management. We also consider Segment EBITDA to be a useful financial measure in evaluating our operating performance, as it provides investors, securities analysts and other interested parties with supplemental information regarding the underlying trends in our ongoing operations. Segment EBITDA includes revenue and expenses that are controllable by the segment. We have presented Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Share as we believe these measures are useful for evaluating the core operating performance of our continuing business across reporting periods and in analyzing our historical operating results. We define Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Share as Net Income and Loss and Diluted Earnings (Loss) per Share adjusted to eliminate the impact of net income and loss attributable to noncontrolling interest, income and loss from discontinued operations, restructuring and transaction related expenses, amortization expense related to all acquired intangible assets, gains and losses on debt extinguishment, changes in fair value of contingent consideration liabilities, other gains and losses related to acquisitions, equity method investments, or divestitures, impairment charges, direct impacts of the Ukraine/Russia conflict, excess tax benefits and deficiencies from stock-based payments and any tax effect of these adjustments. The tax effect of these adjustments is calculated using the effective tax rate for the applicable period or for certain discrete items the specific tax expense or benefit for the adjustment. Given the variability and volatility of the amount of related transactions in a particular period, management believes that these costs are not core operating expenses and should be adjusted in our calculation of Adjusted Net Income. Our adjustment of the amortization of all acquisition-related intangible assets does not exclude the amortization of other assets, which represents expense that is directly attributable to ongoing operations. Management believes that the adjustment relating to amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets supplements the GAAP information with a measure that can be used to assess the comparability of operating performance. The acquired intangible assets were recorded as part of purchase accounting and contribute to revenue generation. Amortization of intangible assets that relate to past acquisitions will recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized. Any future acquisitions may result in the amortization of additional intangible assets. These financial measures are used by management in its decision making and overall evaluation of our operating performance and are included in the metrics used to determine incentive compensation for our senior management.
